question.worked_solution:
Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x),$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x).$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. Therefore, we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Notice that $f(x)={x}^{3}\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}$ is an odd function. Indeed, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =(-x)^{3}\sqrt{4-(-x)^{2}} \\  & =-{x}^{3}\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}} \\  & =-f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

So, because $f(x)={x}^{3}\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}$ is an odd function, we have

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}{x}^{3}\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=0.
$$
